lesson_title: The Wheelbarrow Hidden in Your Pedal
hook_text: A bicycle pedal is a wheelbarrow bent into a circle. Here is why that makes you stronger.
clip_script: Look at a bicycle pedal. An arm sticks out from the axle, with a pedal on the end. That is a crank. Now freeze it. Pivot: the centre of the axle. Effort: your foot on the pedal. Load: the axle surface where the chainring is turned, right next to the centre. Load in the middle, between pivot and effort. That is a second-class lever, same as a wheelbarrow, and second-class levers always make you stronger. Longer arm, stronger push. That is why a village water pump has a handle a metre long. Now bolt a rod to the pedal and a slider to the rod. Turn the crank, the slider goes back and forth. Push the slider, the crank goes round. That is a piston and crankshaft, inside every car engine. One bent lever, and the whole world turns.
visual_style: Whiteboard pedal and axle frozen with pivot, load and effort labelled; a wheelbarrow outline overlays it; a connecting rod and slider attach and animate back and forth.
mood: Aha moment, familiar object made new.
pacing: Pedal frozen and labelled, wheelbarrow comparison, pump handle, crank and slider finale.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the crank, rod and slider in a picture of a car engine.
